info.name: TMDB API Documentation
info.description: # Overview The Movie Database (TMDB) API is a RESTful web service that provides you with access to a rich collection of movie, television, person, and account data. As a developer, you can use the API to search for content, retrieve detailed metadata, manage user accounts, create watchlists, rate media, and build personalized entertainment applications. The API is organized around [REST ](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_State_Transfer) (Representational State Transfer) principles. Meaning, it has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts [form-encoded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/POST_(HTTP)#Use_for_submitting_web_forms) request bodies, returns [JSON-encoded](http://www.json.org/) responses, and uses standard HTTP methods such as **GET**, **POST**, and **DELETE**. In this API documentation guide, you will find practical explanations of 50 TMDB API endpoints, including authentication workflows, account management, movies, TV shows, people, search, lists, ratings, watchlists, and others. Each endpoint includes a clear explanation of the request requirements, parameters, example requests, responses, error handling, and implementation notes to help integrate TMDB efficiently into your applications. ## API versions TMDB currently supports two authentication models: **API v3** and **API v4**. While both versions provide access to TMDB resources, they serve different purposes and use different authentication mechanisms. ### API v3 API v3 is the original TMDB API and remains the most commonly used version for application development. It supports both public data retrieval and authenticated user actions through session-based authentication. For read-only endpoints, requests can be authenticated using a Bearer Token. Endpoints that modify user-specific data (such as creating ratings, managing favorites, or updating watchlists) require a valid **v3 session ID**, which is created through the authentication workflow using a request token approved by the user. This Postman collection primarily uses the **v3 authentication workflow**, including: - Creating a request token - Authenticating the request token - Creating a session ID - Accessing authenticated endpoints using the session ID This approach reflects the authentication flow used throughout the majority of the documented endpoints in this collection. ### API v4 API v4 introduces a modern authentication model designed around user-authorized access tokens. Instead of relying primarily on session-based authentication, v4 uses [OAuth-style](https://oauth.net/2/access-tokens/) token authorization, allowing users to explicitly grant applications permission to access their TMDB account. Some endpoints support converting a user-authorized v4 token into a v3 session, enabling applications to interact with endpoints that still require session-based authentication. However, this workflow requires the user to grant write permissions during the authorization process before the token can be used successfully. Although TMDB supports both authentication models, many user-specific endpoints continue to rely on the v3 session workflow, which is why this collection focuses primarily on API v3 authentication. ## Project scope This collection documents and tests 50 TMDB API endpoints across multiple resource groups, including authentication, search, discover, movies, and networks. Beyond demonstrating successful requests, the documentation also includes parameter explanations, authentication requirements, practical use cases, common error responses, and troubleshooting guidance based on real testing scenarios encountered during implementation. The objective of this project is not only to demonstrate API testing but also to showcase professional API documentation practices that help developers understand, integrate, and troubleshoot the TMDB API effectively. # Getting started Before you begin working with the APIs, complete the following requirements. ## Prerequisite To start using this collection, you need: - A TMDB account. - A valid TMDB API Read Access Token (Bearer Token). - A configured Postman environment with the required variables. - A v3 session ID for endpoints that perform authenticated user actions, such as ratings and account states. If you don't have a registered TMDB account, follow the steps below to get one. This is necessary to get the API Key and API Access Tokens for your API calls. ### **Step 1: Create a TMDB account** - Visit the [TMDB website](https://www.themoviedb.org/signup). - Select **Join TMDB**. - Verify your email address. - Log in to your account with your **Username** and **Password**. ### Step 2: Request an API key After creating your account: - Log in with your credentials and navigate to **Settings**. - Scroll down the menu list on the left-hand side and select **API**. - Scroll to your **API Read Access Token** and **API Key** **Note**: The displayed **API Read Access Token** and **API Key** are the two major credentials you need to make API calls. However, they function differently. Here's the difference. | Credential | Purpose | | --- | --- | | API Read Access Token | Access public TMDB resources | | API Key | Alternative authentication method | With your credentials in hand, you are now ready to make your first API call. ## Store your credentials in an environment variable After you have obtained your **API Key** and **Access Token**, before you start making your API calls, it is advisable to set up an environment variable. The environment variable serves as a placeholder for values that may change or must be reused across several requests. These variables allow you to hold and repeat parameters in requests, collections, scripts, and so on. Meaning, with your credentials in an environment variable, you don't need to hardcode them every time you want to make an API call. Also, if we need to modify a value, you only have to do so in one place. In this collection, we use the following variables: #### Core variables - `{{base_url}}` → Base TMDB API URL - `{{image_base_url}}` → Base URL for image assets #### Authentication variables - `{{access_token}}` → Bearer token for API authentication - `{{session_id}}` → User session ID for account endpoints #### Resource variables - `{{movie_id}}` → Default movie identifier used for testing - `{{tv_id}}` → Default TV show identifier - `{{person_id}}` → Default person identifier #### Optional variables - `{{page}}` → Pagination control - `{{language}}` → Response language To learn more about how to create an environment variable and use it in your API calls, check [this guide](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/websites-apps/explain-the-use-of-environment-variables-in-postman-requests/). ### Base URL All requests are made against the TMDB v3 API: [https://api.themoviedb.org/3](https://api.themoviedb.org/3) ## **Make your first request** ``` bash curl --request GET \ --url "https://api.themoviedb.org/3/movie/550?access_token=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" ``` ``` javascript const response = await fetch( "https://api.themoviedb.org/3/movie/550?access_token=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" ); const movie = await response.json(); console.log(movie); ``` ``` python import requests response = requests.get( "https://api.themoviedb.org/3/movie/550", params={"access_token": "YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN"} ) print(response.json()) ``` ### Example response ``` http 200 OK ``` ``` json { "adult": false, "id": 550, "title": "Fight Club", "original_language": "en", "overview": "A ticking-time-bomb insomniac and a soap salesman channel primal male aggression into a shocking new form of therapy.", "release_date": "1999-10-15", "runtime": 139, "vote_average": 8.4, "vote_count": 30000, "genres": [ { "id": 18, "name": "Drama" } ] } ``` ### Response breakdown | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | adult | boolean | Indicates whether the movie contains adult content. | | id | integer | Unique TMDB identifier for the movie. | | title | string | Movie title. | | original_language | string | Original language of the movie. | | overview | string | Brief summary of the movie. | | release_date | string | Official release date. | | runtime | integer | Movie duration in minutes. | | vote_average | number | Average user rating. | | vote_count | integer | Number of user ratings submitted. | | genres | array | List of genres associated with the movie. | ### What's next? Now that you've successfully retrieved a movie, you can: - Search for movies using the Search API. - Retrieve TV show details. - Explore trending content. - Authenticate a user to access account-specific endpoints such as favorites, ratings, and watchlists.

item.name: Authentication

request.description:
Validates your TMDB API credentials by confirming that the supplied API key or access token is recognized and authorized to access the TMDB API. > Note: You only need your Bearer token or API key for this endpoint. # Example request (API Key) ``` GET {{base_url}}/authentication /validate_key?api_key={{api_key}} ``` Or, if you're using a Bearer token: ``` GET {{base_url}}/authentication/validate_key Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}} ``` # Example success response ``` json { "success": true, "status_code": 1, "status_message": "Success." } ``` # Response fields | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `success` | Indicates whether the supplied credentials are valid. | | `status_code` | TMDB status code describing the result. | | `status_message` | Human-readable description of the validation result. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 7, "status_message": "Invalid API key: You must be granted a valid key." }` | \* Incorrect API key.
\* API key has been revoked.
\* Missing Authorization header.
\* Typographical error in the API key. | \* Verify that the API key is correct.
\* Ensure the Bearer token is valid.
\* Check that the request is sent to the correct API version.
\* Confirm that the Authorization header is properly formatted. | # Common use cases You can use this endpoint for the following tasks: - Verify API credentials during application setup. - Confirm that an API key or access token is valid. - Test API connectivity before making authenticated requests. - Troubleshoot authentication or configuration issues. - Validate credentials in automated deployment or CI/CD pipelines before running API-dependent tasks. **Note**: This endpoint only validates your API credentials. It does not create a user session or authenticate a TMDB user account.

response.name: Validate key

request.description:
Generates a temporary request token used in the TMDB user authentication workflow. > Note: You only need your Bearer token or API key for this endpoint. # Example request Using an API key: ``` GET {{base_url}}/authentication/token/new?api_key={{api_key}} ``` Or using a Bearer token: ``` GET {{base_url}}/authentication/token/new Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}} ``` # Example success response ``` json { "success": true, "expires_at": "2026-06-15 16:12:45 UTC", "request_token": "3c7d8b8c8a5d4f9a8d5e6f7a9b1c2d3e" } ``` # Response fields | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `success` | Boolean | Indicates whether the request completed successfully. | | `expires_at` | String | Date and time when the request token expires. | | `request_token` | String | Temporary token used to obtain user approval and create a session. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 7, "status_message": "Invalid API key: You must be granted a valid key." }` | \* Incorrect API key.
\* API key has been revoked.
\* Missing Authorization header.
\* Typographical error in the API key. | \* Verify that the API key is correct.
\* Ensure the Bearer token is valid.
\* Check that the request is sent to the correct API version.
\* Confirm that the Authorization header is properly formatted. | # Authentication workflow After generating a request token: 1. Open the following URL in your preferred browser: ``` https://www.themoviedb.org/authenticate/{request_token} ``` Replace `{request_token}` with the value returned by this endpoint. 1. Sign in to TMDB (if prompted). 2. Select **Approve** to authorize your application. 3. Use the validated request token to create a user session. # Note - A request token **must be approved** before it can be exchanged for a session ID. - The approval step can be completed in a web browser. - The request token expires after a period of time. If this happens before approval or session creation, generate a new one. - An unapproved or expired request token cannot be used to create a session. Also, a request token alone does not authenticate a user. It simply initiates the authentication process. The complete workflow is: 1. Validate API credentials 2. Create request token 3. Approve the returned token in a web browser 4. Create session 5. Use the session ID to access authenticated endpoints # Common use cases You can use this endpoint for the following tasks: - Start the TMDB user authentication workflow. - Obtain user authorization before creating a session. - Enable access to user-specific endpoints such as Favorites, Watchlists, Ratings, and Account Details. - Authenticate users in applications that require personalized TMDB features.

response.name: Create Request token

request.description:
Creates a v3 `session_id` by exchanging a previously validated request token. The returned ID represents an authenticated TMDB user session and is required to access account-specific endpoints. > **Note**: This endpoint is the final step in the standard TMDB v3 authentication workflow. # Prerequisites Before calling this API, ensure you have: - A valid request token generated using the **Create Request Token** endpoint. - A request token that has been validated through either: - the browser approval flow, or - the **Create Session (with Login)** (`validate_with_login`) endpoint. - A request token that has not expired or already been exchanged for a session. # Request body | Field | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `request_token` | String | Yes | A validated request token obtained during the authentication workflow. | # Example request and body ``` POST {{base_url}}/authentication/session/new ``` ``` json { "request_token": "{{request_token}}" } ``` # Example success response ``` json { "success": true, "session_id": "2d4f3d0d5d4c7e8f9a0b1c2d3e4f5678" } ``` # Response fields | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `success` | Indicates whether the session was created successfully. | | `session_id` | The authenticated user's v3 session ID. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 33, "status_message": "Invalid request token." }` | \* The request token is invalid.
\* The request token has expired.
\* The request token has not been approved or validated.
\* The request token has already been exchanged for a session. | \* Generate a new request token if the current one has expired.
\* Validate the request token using either the browser approval flow or the Create Session (with Login) endpoint.
\* Retry the request using a valid, approved request token. | # Common use cases - Complete the TMDB v3 authentication workflow. - Create an authenticated user session. - Access account-specific endpoints such as Favorites, Watchlists, Ratings, and Account Details. - Maintain an authenticated session across multiple API requests. - Enable personalized features within an application. **Note:** A `session_id` represents an authenticated TMDB user session. Store it securely and reuse it for subsequent authenticated requests instead of creating a new session for every API call. If the user signs out or the session is no longer needed, invalidate it using the **Delete Session** endpoint.

response.name: Create session

request.description:
Creates a temporary guest session and returns a unique ID that allows users who are not signed in to perform supported actions, such as rating movies and TV shows. > Note: Guest sessions are intended for anonymous users and do not provide access to account-specific features such as favorites, watchlists, or account states. Also, guest sessions provide limited permissions and should not be used as a substitute for a standard authenticated user session. ## Example request ``` GET {{base_url}}/authentication/guest_session/new ``` ## Example success response ``` json { "success": true, "guest_session_id": "d5f9b0b2e7c44d5cb8f5b9a1d2e3f456", "expires_at": "2027-01-18 02:41:33 UTC" } ``` ## Response field | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `success` | Indicates whether the guest session was created successfully. | | `guest_session_id` | A unique identifier used to authenticate supported guest actions. | | `expires_at` | The date and time when the guest session expires. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{`
`success": false, "status_code": 3, "status_message": "Authentication failed: You do not have permissions to access the service." }` | \* The Bearer token is missing or invalid.
\* The API Read Access Token has been revoked or is incorrectly configured. | \* Verify that the Authorization header contains a valid Bearer token.
\* Confirm that your TMDB API credentials are active and correctly configured. | # Common use cases - Allow anonymous users to rate movies or TV shows. - Support temporary user interactions without requiring account registration. - Enable quick onboarding experiences by postponing sign-in. - Collect ratings from users who do not wish to create a TMDB account. # Guest session vs. standard user session | Guest session | Standard user session | | --- | --- | | Does not require a TMDB account. | Requires a TMDB account and user authentication. | | Uses a `guest_session_id`. | Uses a `session_id`. | | Supports a limited set of operations, such as rating content. | Supports all authenticated account features. | | Cannot access personal account data. | Can access favorites, watchlists, ratings, account states, and custom lists. | | Intended for anonymous users. | Intended for authenticated users. | The diagram below further expatiates on this:

response.name: Create Guest session

request.description:
Creates a v3 `session_id` using a user-authorized v4 access token. > **Note:** Unlike the standard **Create Session** endpoint, which exchanges a validated request token for a session, this endpoint creates a v3 session directly from a user-authorized v4 access token. Therefore, it is intended for applications that use the TMDB v4 authentication flow but still need a v3 session to access endpoints that require session-based authentication. # Prerequisites Before calling this API, ensure you have: - A valid user-authorized v4 access token. - A v4 access token with write permission. > **Note:** Do not use your standard TMDB **Read Access Token**, as it is intended for application authentication and cannot be exchanged for a v3 session. # Example request ``` POST {{base_url}}/authentication/session/convert/4 Authorization: Bearer {{v4_access_token}} ``` # Example success response ``` json { "success": true, "session_id": "c8d7b9b0d7d0c0b6c0d5f2..." } ``` # Response fields | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `success` | Indicates whether the session was created successfully. | | `session_id` | The newly created v3 session ID. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 36, "status_message": "This token hasn't been granted write permission by the user." }` | \* A standard TMDB Read Access Token was supplied instead of a user-authorized v4 access token.
\* The v4 access token has not been granted write permission by the user.
\* The supplied access token is invalid or has expired. | \* Create a new v4 request token.
\* Ask the user to authorize the token through the TMDB authorization flow.
\* Exchange the approved request token for a user-authorized v4 access token.
\* Retry the request using the authorized access token. | # Note - This endpoint is intended for applications using the TMDB v4 authentication workflow. - The supplied v4 access token must be authorized and include write permission. - A standard TMDB Read Access Token cannot be used to create a v3 session. - The returned `session_id` can be used with any v3 endpoint that requires session-based authentication. Also, most applications using only the TMDB v3 API do not need this endpoint. Use **Create Session** if you are following the standard v3 authentication workflow. This endpoint is primarily intended for applications that authenticate users through the TMDB v4 API but need to interact with v3 endpoints that require a `session_id`. # Common use cases You can use the create session (from v4 token) for the following tasks: - Convert an authenticated v4 user session into a v3 session. - Access v3 endpoints that require a `session_id`. - Support applications that integrate both the TMDB v3 and v4 APIs. - Reuse an existing authenticated v4 user session without repeating the v3 authentication workflow. Tip: TMDB provides two different Bearer tokens, and they are not interchangeable: | Token | Purpose | | --- | --- | | **Read Access Token** | Authenticates your application for public API requests. It cannot create a v3 session. | | **User-authorized v4 Access Token** | Represents an authenticated TMDB user and can be exchanged for a v3 `session_id` using this endpoint. | If you receive **Status Code 36**, the most common cause is that you're using the standard **Read Access Token** instead of a user-authorized v4 access token with write permission.

response.name: Create Session (from v4 token)

request.description:
Validates a previously generated request token using a TMDB username and password. # Prerequisites Before calling this endpoint, ensure you have: 1. A valid request token generated using the **Create Request Token** endpoint. 2. A valid TMDB username and password for the user. 3. A request token that has not expired. > **Note**: Once the request token has been successfully validated, it can be exchanged for a v3 session ID, allowing your application to access authenticated, user-specific resources such as account details, favorites, watchlists, ratings, and account states. Unlike the browser-based approval flow, this endpoint validates the request token programmatically by submitting the user's TMDB credentials directly to the API. # Request body | Field | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `username` | String | Yes | The user's TMDB username. | | `password` | String | Yes | The user's TMDB password. | | `request_token` | String | Yes | The request token returned by the Create Request Token endpoint. | # Browser approval vs. `validate_with_login` Both methods validate a request token before it is exchanged for a session ID. | Browser approval | `validate_with_login` | | --- | --- | | User approves the request token on the TMDB website. | User submits TMDB username and password directly to the API. | | No user credentials pass through your application. | User credentials are included in the request body. | | May redirect the user to TMDB. | Validation occurs entirely through the API. | | Returns a validated request token. | Returns a validated request token. | Both approaches produce the same result: a validated request token that can be used to create a session. # Example request ``` POST {{base_url}}/authentication/token/validate_with_login ``` ``` { "username": "your_username", "password": "your_password", "request_token": "{{request_token}}" } ``` # Example success response ``` json { "success": true, "expires_at": "2026-06-15 16:12:45 UTC", "request_token": "3c7d8b8c8a5d4f9a8d5e6f7a9b1c2d3e" } ``` # Response fields | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `success` | Indicates whether the request token was successfully validated. | | `expires_at` | The expiration date and time of the validated request token. | | `request_token` | The validated request token that can be exchanged for a session ID. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 30, "status_message": "Invalid username and/or password." }` | \* Incorrect TMDB username.
\* Incorrect TMDB password.
\* Expired request token.
\* Request token has already been used or is invalid. | \* Verify the user's TMDB credentials.
\* Generate a new request token if the existing one has expired.
\* Retry the validation request before creating a session. | # Common use cases - Validate a request token without redirecting users to the TMDB website. - Support server-side authentication workflows. - Authenticate users before creating a session. - Prepare a validated request token for the **Create Session** endpoint. # Note - This endpoint **does not create a session ID**. - A successfully validated request token must be passed to the **Create Session** endpoint to obtain a `session_id`. - If the request token expires before a session is created, generate a new token and repeat the validation process. - Once a request token has been successfully exchanged for a session, it cannot be reused.

response.name: Create session (with login)

request.description:
Deletes an active v3 session, immediately invalidating the associated `session_id`. > **Note**: Before calling this endpoint, ensure that you have a valid `session_id` that has not already expired. Also, once the session has been deleted, it can no longer be used to access authenticated TMDB endpoints that require session-based authentication. # Request body | Field | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `session_id` | String | Yes | The active session ID to delete. | # Example request and body ``` DELETE {{base_url}}/authentication/session ``` ``` { "session_id": "{{session_id}}" } ``` # Example success response ``` json { "success": true } ``` # Response fields | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `success` | Indicates whether the session was successfully deleted. If true, it means the session has been successfully deleted. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{ success": false, "status_code": 3, "status_message": "Authentication failed: You do not have permissions to access the service." }` | \* The provided **session_id** is invalid.
\* The session has already expired.
\* The request contains an incorrect or malformed session ID. | \* Verify that the **session_id** is valid.
\* Generate a new session if the existing session has expired.
\* Ensure the session ID is correctly referenced from the Postman environment. | # Note - Deleting a session immediately invalidates the associated `session_id`. - Once deleted, the session cannot be restored or reused. - To access authenticated endpoints again, you must complete the authentication workflow and create a new session. - Deleting a session signs the user out of your application but does not revoke the user's TMDB account or API credentials. # Common use cases - Sign a user out of an application. - End an authenticated session after account operations are complete. - Invalidate sessions that are no longer needed. - Improve application security by preventing reuse of an active session. - Support logout functionality across web and mobile applications. Tip: Deleting a session only invalidates the current **v3 session**. If the user wants to continue using authenticated endpoints such as **Favorites**, **Watchlists**, or **Ratings**, your application must create a new session by repeating the authentication workflow, which includes: 1. Create a request token. 2. Validate the request token (browser approval or `validate_with_login`). 3. Create a new session. 4. Use the new `session_id` for subsequent authenticated requests.

response.name: Delete session

request.description:
Returns account metadata, including the account identifier required by many account-specific requests. > **Note**: Before calling this endpoint, you need a valid `session_id` that has not already expired. The session_id must be generated through the TMDB authentication workflow. Requests made with an invalid or expired session ID will return an authentication error. ### Example request #### cURL ``` bash curl --request GET \ --url "https://api.themoviedb.org/3/account?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY&session_id=YOUR_SESSION_ID" ``` #### Request body ``` json { "session_id": "{{session_id}}" } ``` #### Response ``` json { "avatar": {}, "id": 12345678, "iso_639_1": "en", "iso_3166_1": "US", "name": "John Doe", "username": "johndoe"} ``` ### Response field | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | id | Unique account identifier used in account endpoints. | | username | Account username. | | name | Display name associated with the account. | | iso_639_1 | Preferred language code. | | iso_3166_1 | Preferred country code. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 403 | Forbidden | Unexpected HTML Response | \* Missing or invalid session_id.
\* Missing API key or Bearer token.
\* Incorrect request URL.
\* Temporary CloudFront or routing issue. | \* Verify that the session_id is valid and has not expired.
\* Confirm that the request includes the required authentication.
\* Ensure the request is sent to:
GET /3/account
\* Retry the request if the issue is caused by a temporary service interruption. | > **Note**: Alternatively, you can run this link ([https://api.themoviedb.org/3/account?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY&session_id=YOUR_SESSION_ID)](https://urlhttps://api.themoviedb.org/3/account?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY&session_id=YOUR_SESSION_ID) in your web browser; only fill out your actual API Key and Session ID. ### Common use cases - Retrieve the authenticated user's TMDB `account_id` required for subsequent account-related API requests. - Confirm that the authentication workflow has successfully established access to the user's account. - Use the returned account information when working with endpoints such as Favorites, Watchlists, Ratings, and Account Details. Now that you have gotten the necessary IDs and tokens, let's proceed to other endpoints where we will use them.

item.description: TMDB supports two primary authentication types: 1. API key or token authentication 2. User authentication The API key and API token are two different credentials you get from TMDB once you register your account. Attaching the Key or Token to your request is very important. But whether or not you need to include the user authentication information depends on the resource you want to access. Note: If you don't have an account, complete the steps in **Getting started** to create a developer account and register an application. ## API key or token authentication The API Key or Access Token identifies your application when communicating with TMDB. It is the simplest way to access TMDB data. However, it only provides [read access](https://www.twingate.com/blog/glossary/read-access) to public TMDB resources but does not grant access to user-specific account data. With a valid API key or token, you can retrieve publicly available information such as movie details and search results. ### Example request ``` GET /movie/550?access_token=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN ``` ### Example cURL request ``` bash curl --request GET \ --url "https://api.themoviedb.org/3/movie/550?access_token=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" ``` > **Note**: The key or token should be stored securely and never exposed in public repositories. ## User authentication User authentication is required when interacting with resources that belong to a specific TMDB user account. Unlike API key or token authentication, user authentication allows you to perform actions on behalf of a user, such as creating watchlists and retrieving account-specific data. ### Authentication workflow User authentication requires the following components: | Credential | Purpose | | --- | --- | | Request Token | Temporary token used to authorize a user | | Session ID | Authenticated session identifier | | Account ID | Unique identifier for a TMDB account | The authentication process follows this sequence: ``` text Create Request Token ↓ Approve Request Token ↓ Create Session ↓ Retrieve Account Details ↓ Access Protected Resources ``` Once a valid session has been established, the session ID and account ID can be used to access protected account endpoints. ### Example protected request ``` http GET /account/{account_id}/favorite/movies ``` ### Example cURL request ``` bash curl --request GET \ --url "https://api.themoviedb.org/3/account/{account_id}/favorite/movies?access_token=YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN&session_id=YOUR_SESSION_ID" ``` ### Important notes - User authentication requires a valid API key or token. - Session IDs are required for all account-specific endpoints. - Account IDs are used to identify the account associated with the request. - Session IDs may become invalid and require reauthentication. For a complete walkthrough of the authentication workflow, check the next section to see how each endpoint works.

request.description:
Retrieves the public profile information for a specified TMDB account. ## Prerequisite - Before calling this endpoint, ensure you have: - Authenticated with the TMDB API using your Bearer token. - Completed the authentication workflow to obtain a valid `session_id`. - Retrieved your `account_id` using the **Get Account Details** endpoint in the **Authentication** collection (`GET /account`). - Used the returned `account_id` as the path parameter for this endpoint. > **Note**: This endpoint is typically called after the account ID has been obtained and is used to access additional account profile information. ## Path parameter | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `account_id` | Integer | Yes | The unique identifier of the TMDB account whose details are being retrieved. | # Example request ``` GET {{base_url}}/account/{{account_id}}?session_id={{session_id}} ``` # Example success response ``` json { "avatar": { "gravatar": { "hash": "205e460b479e2e5b48aec07710c08d50" }, "tmdb": { "avatar_path": "/abc123.jpg" } }, "id": 218, "iso_639_1": "en", "iso_3166_1": "US", "name": "John Doe", "include_adult": false, "username": "johndoe" } ``` # Response fields | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `id` | Unique TMDB account identifier. | | `username` | TMDB username. | | `name` | Display name associated with the account. | | `avatar` | Avatar information, including Gravatar and TMDB avatar details. | | `iso_639_1` | Preferred language for the account. | | `iso_3166_1` | Preferred country or region. | | `include_adult` | Indicates whether adult content is enabled for the account. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example Response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{`
`success": false, "status_code": 3, "status_message": "Authentication failed: You do not have permissions to access the service." }` | \* The session_id is invalid or has expired.
\* The session_id does not belong to the specified account.
\* The Bearer token is missing or invalid. | \* Verify that a valid session_id is included in the request.
\* Ensure the session_id was created through the TMDB authentication workflow.
\* Confirm that the supplied account_id corresponds to the authenticated session. | | 404 | Not found | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 34, "status_message": "The resource you requested could not be found." }` | \* The specified account_id does not exist.
\* The account_id is invalid or incorrectly formatted. | Retrieve the correct account_id from the Authentication collection before retrying the request. | # Common use cases - Retrieve a user's profile information. - Obtain account preferences such as language and region. - Display account details in an application. - Verify the authenticated account before performing account-specific operations. - Retrieve account metadata required by other Account endpoints.

Adds or removes a movie or TV show from an authenticated user's favorites. # Prerequisites Before calling this endpoint, ensure that you have: 1. Completed the TMDB authentication workflow. 2. Obtained a valid `session_id`. 3. Retrieved the authenticated user's `account_id`. 4. Identified the TMDB ID of the movie or TV show you want to update. # Path parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `account_id` | Integer | Yes | The unique identifier of the authenticated TMDB account. | # Query parameters | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `session_id` | String | Yes | The authenticated user's session identifier. | # Request body | Field | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `media_type` | String | Yes | The type of media. Accepted values are `movie` and `tv`. | | `media_id` | Integer | Yes | The TMDB identifier of the movie or TV show. | | `favorite` | Boolean | Yes | Determines whether the item is added to (`true`) or removed from (`false`) the favorites list. | # Example request **Add a movie to favorites** ``` POST {{base_url}}/account/{{account_id}}/favorite?session_id={{session_id}} ``` ``` json { "media_type": "movie", "media_id": 550, "favorite": true } ``` **Remove a movie from favorites** ``` POST {{base_url}}/account/{{account_id}}/favorite?session_id={{session_id}} ``` ``` json { "media_type": "movie", "media_id": 550, "favorite": false } ``` # Example success response ``` json { "success": true, "status_code": 1, "status_message": "Success." } ``` ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 400 | Bad request | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 18, "status_message": "Validation failed." }` | \* Missing media_type.
\* Missing media_id.
\* Missing favorite.
Invalid media_type (must be movie or tv).
\* Invalid or malformed JSON request body. | Ensure that all required request body fields are present, media_type is either movie or tv, and the JSON body is properly formatted. | | 401 | Unauthorized | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 3, "status_message": "Authentication failed: You do not have permissions to access the service." }` | \* Missing or invalid session_id.
\* Expired session.
\* Missing or invalid Bearer token.
\* The session_id does not belong to the specified account. | Verify that the Bearer token is valid, the session_id is active, and the supplied account_id matches the authenticated user. | # Common use cases - Allow users to save favorite movies. - Allow users to save favorite TV shows. - Build personalized user profiles. - Synchronize favorite content across multiple devices. - Create "My Favorites" sections within an application. **Note**: This endpoint is **idempotent** with respect to the `favorite` field. Sending the same request multiple times with the same value (for example, `favorite: true` for an item that is already favorited) does not create duplicate entries. Likewise, setting `favorite` to `false` for an item that is not currently in the favorites list ensures it is not marked as a favorite. item.description:
This collection contains endpoints for accessing and managing user-specific data within The Movie Database (TMDB) API. With these endpoints, you can retrieve account information, access user activity, manage favorite movies and TV shows, maintain watchlists, submit and remove ratings, and interact with other account-related resources.

Depending on the operation being performed, requests may require a valid **v3 session ID**, an **account ID**, or both.

### Prerequisite

You need the following authentication model to securely and successfully use the endpoints in this collection:

| Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Bearer token or API key** | Required for all account endpoints. |
| **v3 Session ID** | Required for endpoints that access or modify user-specific data. |
| **Account ID** | Required for endpoints that identify which account the request targets. |

Therefore, before testing the endpoints in this collection, ensure you

1. Validate your API key or token.
    
2. Create a request token.
    
3. Validate the request token.
    
4. Create a v3 session.
    
5. Call GET /account.
    
6. Copy the returned ID.
    
7. Save it as {{account_id}}.
    
8. Test the remaining Account endpoints.
    

Note: Store all values as Postman environment variables for use throughout this collection.

### Purpose

The Account endpoints can perform the following operations:

- Retrieve account profile information.
    
- View account-specific movie and TV states.
    
- Manage favorite movies and TV shows.
    
- Add or remove items from a watchlist.
    
- Submit and delete movie and TV ratings.
    
- Retrieve rated, favorite, and watchlisted content.
    
- Access user-specific account activity.
    

Now let's get into the endpoints to see how they work.

\* Invalid or revoked API key.
\* Incorrectly formatted Authorization header. | \* Verify that a valid Bearer token or API key is included in the request and that the authentication credentials have not expired or been revoked. | # Common use cases - Display movie age ratings in an application. - Filter movie results by certification using the **Discover Movies** endpoint. - Build parental control or age-restriction features. - Interpret certification values returned by movie-related endpoints. - Configure region-specific content filtering. # Note - This endpoint does not require a `movie_id`. - Certification ratings are grouped by ISO 3166-1 country codes (for example, `US`, `GB`, `DE`, and `FR`). - Certification systems vary by country, so the available ratings differ between regions. - The returned certification values can be used with endpoints such as **Discover Movies** to filter content based on regional age ratings. Tip: This endpoint returns the available movie certification systems used by each country—it does not return the certification assigned to a specific movie. For example: - Calling this endpoint tells you that the United States uses certifications such as **G**, **PG**, **PG-13**, and **R**. - To retrieve the certification assigned to a particular movie, use the **Movie Release Dates** endpoint, which returns country-specific release information along with the movie's certification.

request.description:
The **TV Certifications** endpoint retrieves an up-to-date list of officially supported TV show certifications on TMDB.

## Prerequisites

Before calling this endpoint, ensure that you have:

1. The `base_url` environment variable configured correctly.
    
2. The Authorization header configured with your valid Bearer token.
    

### Example request

``` text
GET {{base_url}}/certification/tv/list

 ```

## Response

A successful request returns a `200 OK` response containing a `certifications` object.

The `certifications` object is organized by country or region code. Each country contains an array of certification objects.

### Response fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `certifications` | Object | Contains TV certification lists grouped by country or region code. |
| `certifications.{country_code}` | Array | Contains the certifications supported in the specified country or region. |
| `certification` | String | The certification or rating code. |
| `meaning` | String | Describes what the certification means. |
| `order` | Integer | Indicates the certification's order within the country's rating system. |

### Example response structure

``` json
{
  "certifications": {
    "US": [
      {
        "certification": "TV-Y",
        "meaning": "This program is designed to be appropriate for all children.",
        "order": 1
      },
      {
        "certification": "TV-Y7",
        "meaning": "This program is designed for children age 7 and above.",
        "order": 2
      },
      {
        "certification": "TV-G",
        "meaning": "Most parents would find this program suitable for all ages.",
        "order": 3
      }
    ]
  }
}

 ```

**Note:** The endpoint returns certification data for multiple countries and regions. The available certification codes and their meanings vary by country.

## Common use case

Use this endpoint when your application needs to:

- Display available TV content ratings.
    
- Build a TV certification or parental-control filter.
    
- Map TMDB TV certification codes to user-facing descriptions.
    
- Retrieve the rating systems supported for different countries or regions.
    

## Notes

- The endpoint returns certification information rather than individual TV shows.
    
- Certification data is grouped by country or region.
    
- The certification list may be updated as TMDB updates its supported rating systems.

response.name: TV Certifications

item.description:
The **Certifications** collection provides region-specific content ratings for movies and TV shows. These certifications help applications determine the appropriate audience for a title based on the content rating systems used in different countries.

Unlike movie details or search endpoints, certification endpoints return reference data that changes infrequently and can be reused across multiple API requests.

# Authentication

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Bearer Token | Recommended |
| Session ID | Not Required |

The endpoints in this collection are public, read-only, and do not require an authenticated user session.

# Available endpoints

There are only two endpoints in this collection. The table below briefly explain them.

| Endpoint | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Get Movie Certifications** | Returns certification ratings used for movies, grouped by country. |
| **Get TV Certifications** | Returns certification ratings used for TV shows, grouped by country. |

# Example request

``` bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://api.themoviedb.org/3/certification/movie/list' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN' \
  --header 'accept: application/json'

 ```

# Example response

``` json
{
  "certifications": {
    "US": [
      {
        "certification": "G",
        "meaning": "All ages admitted.",
        "order": 1
      },
      {
        "certification": "PG",
        "meaning": "Parental guidance suggested.",
        "order": 2
      },
      {
        "certification": "PG-13",
        "meaning": "Parents strongly cautioned.",
        "order": 3
      },
      {
        "certification": "R",
        "meaning": "Restricted.",
        "order": 4
      }
    ],
    "GB": [
      {
        "certification": "U",
        "meaning": "Suitable for all.",
        "order": 1
      }
    ]
  }
}

 ```

# Response fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `certifications` | Object | Contains certification ratings grouped by country. |
| `certifications.` | Array | List of certifications for a specific country or region. |
| `certification` | String | The content rating assigned within the country's rating system (for example, `PG-13` or `R`). |
| `meaning` | String | A human-readable explanation of the certification. |
| `order` | Integer | The relative position of the certification within that country's rating hierarchy. Lower values generally represent less restrictive ratings. |

# Understanding the response

Each property inside the `certifications` object represents an **ISO 3166-1 country code**.

For example:

- `US` → United States
    
- `GB` → United Kingdom
    
- `CA` → Canada
    
- `AU` → Australia
    

Each country contains its own array of certification ratings because age classification systems vary between regions.

For example:

```
{
  "certification": "PG-13",
  "meaning": "Parents strongly cautioned.",
  "order": 3
}

 ```

This indicates that, within the United States rating system, the movie has received a **PG-13** certification, meaning some material may be inappropriate for children under 13 years of age.

# Purpose

The certification endpoint can be used for the following operations

- Display age ratings in movie and TV applications.
    
- Filter content based on parental control settings.
    
- Implement region-specific content restrictions.
    
- Display localized certification information to users.
    
- Support compliance with regional content classification standards.
    

# Note

- Certification systems differ from country to country. For example, a movie rated **PG-13** in the United States may receive a different certification in the United Kingdom or Australia.
    
- These endpoints return reference data rather than information about a specific movie or TV show.
    
- To retrieve the certification assigned to an individual movie, use the **Movie Release Dates** endpoint, which includes country-specific certifications alongside release information.
    
- Because certification data changes infrequently, applications may cache these responses to reduce the number of API requests.
    

Tip: The **Certifications** endpoints define the available rating systems used in each country—they do not indicate the rating assigned to a specific movie or TV show.

request.description:
Searches TMDB across multiple resource types in a single request. Unlike the individual Search endpoints, which return results for a single resource type, the Multi Search endpoint searches **movies**, **TV shows**, and **people** simultaneously using a single search query. ## Query parameter | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `query` | String | Yes | The name or keyword used to search for movie collections. Searches are performed against original, translated, and alternative collection names. | `Tom-Cruise` | | `language` | String | No | Specifies the language of the returned results. | `en-US` | | `page` | Integer | No | Returns a specific page of search results. | `1` | | `include_adult` | String | No | Indicates whether it includes adult content. | `false` | ### Example request ``` {{base_url}}/search/multi?query=Tom-Cruise&language=en-US&page=1&include_adult=false ``` ## Example success response ``` json { "page": 1, "results": [ { "media_type": "movie", "id": 27205, "title": "Inception" }, { "media_type": "person", "id": 500, "name": "Tom Cruise" }, { "media_type": "tv", "id": 1399, "name": "Game of Thrones" } ], "total_pages": 1, "total_results": 3 } ``` ## Response field | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `page` | Integer | The current page of search results. | | `results` | Array | An array containing movies, TV shows, and people that match the search query. | | `results[].media_type` | String | Identifies the type of result. Possible values include `movie`, `tv`, and `person`. | | `results[].id` | Integer | The unique TMDB identifier of the returned movie, TV show, or person. | | `results[].title` | String | The title of a movie result. This field is present when `media_type` is `movie`. | | `results[].name` | String | The name of a TV show or person. This field is present when `media_type` is `tv` or `person`. | | `total_pages` | Integer | The total number of pages available for the search results. | | `total_results` | Integer | The total number of results matching the search query across the supported media types. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 400 | Bad Request | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 22, "status_message": "Invalid parameter: query must be provided." }` | \* The query parameter is missing.
\* The query parameter is empty.
\* The request contains an invalid query value. | Provide a valid search term in the query parameter and retry the request. | # Common use cases - Implement a global search feature across multiple media types. - Build search bars that display movies, TV shows, and people together. - Reduce the number of API requests by searching multiple resource types at once. - Provide users with comprehensive search results from a single query. # Note - Each result includes a `media_type` field indicating whether the resource is a `movie`, `tv`, or `person`. - Results are paginated and support the `page` query parameter. - Use the returned TMDB IDs with the corresponding Movie, TV, or People endpoints to retrieve additional information.

request.description:
Searches TMDB people by name. A person represents an individual involved in the film or television industry, such as an actor, director, producer, writer, or other crew member. ## Query parameter | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `query` | String | Yes | The name or keyword used to search for movie collections. Searches are performed against original, translated, and alternative collection names. | `Inception` | | `language` | String | No | Specifies the language of the returned results. | `en-US` | | `page` | Integer | No | Returns a specific page of search results. | `1` | | `include_adult` | String | No | Indicates whether it includes adult content. | `false` | ### Example request ``` {{base_url}}/search/person?query=Tom-Cruise&language=en-US&page=1&include_adult=false ``` ## Example success response ``` json { "page": 1, "results": [ { "id": 500, "name": "Tom Cruise", "known_for_department": "Acting", "popularity": 87.3, "profile_path": "/profile.jpg" } ], "total_pages": 1, "total_results": 1 } ``` ## Response field | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `page` | Integer | The current page number. | | `results` | Array | An array containing the matching person results. | | `results[].id` | Integer | The unique TMDB ID of the person. | | `results[].name` | String | The person's name. | | `results[].known_for_department` | String | The department the person is primarily known for. | | `results[].popularity` | Number | The person's popularity score on TMDB. | | `results[].profile_path` | String / null | The relative path to the person's profile image. | | `total_pages` | Integer | The total number of pages available. | | `total_results` | Integer | The total number of matching people. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 400 | Bad Request | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 22, "status_message": "Invalid parameter: query must be provided." }` | \* The query parameter is missing.
\* The query parameter is empty.
\* The request contains an invalid query value. | Provide a valid person's name in the query parameter and retry the request. | # Common use case - Search for actors, directors, writers, and other entertainment professionals. - Build autocomplete or search functionality for people. - Retrieve a person's TMDB ID for use with the People endpoints. - Display cast and crew search results within an application. # Note - Returns matching people based on the supplied search term. - Results are paginated and support the `page` query parameter. - Each result includes a unique TMDB person ID that can be used with the People collection to retrieve additional details. - Search results may include actors, actresses, directors, producers, writers, composers, and other entertainment professionals. Tip: Use the returned ID value with the **People** collection to retrieve detailed information about a person, including their biography, movie and TV credits, images, external IDs, and social media links (where available).

Searches are performed against original, translated, and alternative collection names. | `Breaking Bad` | | `language` | String | No | Specifies the language of the returned results. | `en-US` | | `page` | Integer | No | Returns a specific page of search results. | `1` | | `include_adult` | String | No | Indicates whether it includes adult content. | `false` | | `first_air_date_year` | String | No | Filters results by the TV show's first air date year. | `2008` | ### Example request ``` {{base_url}}/search/tv?query=Breaking Bad&language=en-US&page=1&include_adult=false ``` ## Example success response ``` json { "page": 1, "results": [ { "id": 1396, "name": "Breaking Bad", "first_air_date": "2008-01-20", "overview": "A high school chemistry teacher diagnosed with cancer...", "vote_average": 8.9, "popularity": 315.8 } ], "total_pages": 1, "total_results": 1 } ``` ## Response field | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `page` | Integer | The current page number. | | `results` | Array | An array containing the matching TV show results. | | `results[].id` | Integer | The unique TMDB ID of the TV show. | | `results[].name` | String | The name of the TV show. | | `results[].first_air_date` | String | The date the TV show first aired, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. | | `results[].overview` | String | A brief description or synopsis of the TV show. | | `results[].vote_average` | Number | The average user rating for the TV show. | | `results[].popularity` | Number | The popularity score of the TV show on TMDB. | | `total_pages` | Integer | The total number of pages available. | | `total_results` | Integer | The total number of matching TV shows. | ## Endpoint-specific error | **Error status** | **Description** | Example response | **Possible causes** | Solution | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 400 | Bad Request | `{ "success": false, "status_code": 22, "status_message": "Invalid parameter: query must be provided." }` | \* The query parameter is missing.
\* The query parameter is empty.
\* The request contains an invalid query value. | Provide a valid TV show name or keyword in the query parameter and retry the request. | ## Common use cases - Allow users to search for TV shows by name. - Provide matching TV show suggestions as users type. - Show titles, release dates, overviews, ratings, and popularity scores. - Use the returned TMDB ID to retrieve additional information about a selected show. - Help users find TV shows based on search queries.EndFragment # Note - Searches across original, translated, and alternative TV show names. - Results are returned in a paginated format and support the `page` query parameter. - Optional parameters such as `language`, `first_air_date_year`, `include_adult`, and `page` can be used to refine search results. - Each result includes a unique TMDB TV series ID that can be used with the TV collection to retrieve detailed information.

item.description:
The Search collection contains endpoints that allow you to query TMDB’s database to find movies, TV shows, or people based on a text input. It supports multiple search types (movies, TV, people, and multi-search) and returns relevant results with metadata such as titles, names, release dates, and popularity scores, making it useful for building dynamic search features in applications.

> **Note:** Search endpoints only need your Bearer Token or API Key to access data. The endpoints access publicly available TMDB data and do not require a `session_id` or `account_id`. 
  

## Purpose

The Search collection supports the following operations:

- Search for movies by title or keyword.
    
- Search for TV shows by name.
    
- Search for people, including actors, directors, and other contributors.
    
- Perform a multi-search across movies, TV shows, and people in a single request.
    
- Retrieve paginated search results.
    
- Refine search results using optional query parameters.
    

## Common query parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | Yes | The text used to search for matching resources. |
| `language` | No | Specifies the language of the returned results. |
| `page` | No | Returns a specific page of search results. |
| `include_adult` | No | Determines whether adult content is included in the results. |
| `region` | No | Filters results based on a specific country or region (supported by certain endpoints). |

## Quick reference

| If you want to... | Use this endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| Search for a movie | `GET /search/movie` |
| Search for a TV show | `GET /search/tv` |
| Search for an actor, director, or other contributor | `GET /search/person` |
| Search for a movie franchise or series | `GET /search/collection` |
| Search for a production company | `GET /search/company` |
| Search for descriptive content tags | `GET /search/keyword` |
| Search across movies, TV shows, and people with one request | `GET /search/multi` |

# Common use cases

The Search collection is best used for the following functionalities:

- Build search features for finding movies, TV shows, and people.
    
- Allow users to search across multiple types of TMDB content from a single interface.
    
- Provide content discovery features based on movie titles, TV show names, or people's names.
    
- Display relevant search results with basic information about each matching resource.
    
- Retrieve the TMDB IDs of movies, TV shows, or people for use with other API collections.
    
- Build unified search experiences that combine different content types.
    
- Support localized search experiences by using language and region parameters where available.
    
- Help users discover content when they know only part of a title or person's name.

item.name: Discover

request.description:
Discovers movies by applying one or more filtering and sorting criteria instead of a search query.

## Common query parameters

| Parameter | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | Specifies the language of the returned results. | `en-US` |
| `sort_by` | Sorts the results using a supported sort option. | `popularity.desc` |
| `page` | Returns a specific page of results. | `1` |
| `with_genres` | Filters movies by one or more genre IDs. | `28,12` |
| `primary_release_year` | Filters movies by release year. | `2025` |
| `vote_average.gte` | Returns movies with at least the specified average rating. | `7.5` |
| `vote_count.gte` | Returns movies with at least the specified number of votes. | `100` |
| `with_original_language` | Filters movies by their original language. | `en` |
| `with_watch_providers` | Filters movies available from specific streaming providers. | `8` |
| `watch_region` | Specifies the country used for watch provider filtering. | `US` |

``` bash
curl --request GET \
  --url '{{base_url}}/discover/movie?with_genres=28&primary_release_year=2025&sort_by=popularity.desc'

 ```

## Example response

``` json
{
  "page": 1,
  "results": [
    {
      "adult": false,
      "backdrop_path": "/1RgPyOhN4DRs225BGTlHJqCudII.jpg",
      "genre_ids": [16, 28, 14],
      "id": 1311031,
      "title": "Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba Infinity Castle",
      "original_language": "ja",
      "original_title": "劇場版「鬼滅の刃」無限城編 第一章 猗窩座再来",
      "overview": "The Demon Slayer Corps are drawn into the Infinity Castle...",
      "popularity": 94.8947,
      "poster_path": "/fWVSwgjpT2D78VUh6X8UBd2rorW.jpg",
      "release_date": "2025-07-18",
      "softcore": false,
      "video": false,
      "vote_average": 7.737,
      "vote_count": 896
    }
  ],
  "total_pages": 98,
  "total_results": 1948
}

 ```

# Response field

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | Integer | The current page number. |
| `results` | Array | Contains movies that match the specified filters. |
| `results[].adult` | Boolean | Indicates whether the movie is classified as adult content. |
| `results[].backdrop_path` | String / null | The relative path to the movie's backdrop image. |
| `results[].genre_ids` | Array | Contains the TMDB genre IDs associated with the movie. |
| `results[].id` | Integer | The unique TMDB ID of the movie. |
| `results[].title` | String | The movie's title. |
| `results[].original_language` | String | The original language of the movie. |
| `results[].original_title` | String | The movie's original title. |
| `results[].overview` | String | A brief description of the movie. |
| `results[].popularity` | Number | The movie's popularity score on TMDB. |
| `results[].poster_path` | String / null | The relative path to the movie's poster image. |
| `results[].release_date` | String | The movie's release date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. |
| `results[].softcore` | Boolean | Indicates whether the movie is classified as softcore content. |
| `results[].video` | Boolean | Indicates whether the movie is a video. |
| `results[].vote_average` | Number | The average user rating for the movie. |
| `results[].vote_count` | Integer | The number of votes received by the movie. |
| `total_pages` | Integer | The total number of pages available. |
| `total_results` | Integer | The total number of movies matching the specified filters. |

# Advanced filtering

The Discover Movies endpoint supports combining multiple filters to create highly targeted queries.

For example, you can retrieve:

- Action movies released in **2024**.
    
- Movies with an average rating of **8.0 or higher**.
    
- Movies available on a specific streaming provider.
    
- Movies in a particular language or region.
    
- Family-friendly movies based on certification.
    
- Highly rated movies with a minimum number of user votes.
    

# Region-based release dates

When the `region` parameter is supplied, TMDB uses the movie's **regional release date** instead of its primary release date.

If the `with_release_type` parameter is also specified, the returned release date is determined by the order of the requested release types.

For example:

- `with_release_type=2|3` prioritizes the **limited theatrical** release before the **wide theatrical** release.
    
- `with_release_type=3|2` prioritizes the **wide theatrical** release before the **limited theatrical** release.
    

This behavior is useful when building applications that display release dates specific to a particular country or release strategy.

# AND / OR filter logic

Several filtering parameters support combining multiple values using commas (`,`) or pipes (`|`).

| Separator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `,` | **AND** — results must satisfy **all** specified values. | `with_genres=28,12` |
| \` | \` | **OR** — results may satisfy **any** of the specified values. |

For example:

- `with_genres=28,12` returns movies classified as **both Action and Adventure**.
    
- `with_genres=28\|12` returns movies classified as **Action or Adventure**.
    

Using this logic allows developers to create more flexible and precise discovery queries.

# Common use cases

- Build **Browse Movies** pages.
    
- Recommend movies based on user preferences.
    
- Filter movies by genre, language, certification, or streaming provider.
    
- Display popular, top-rated, or recently released movies.
    
- Create advanced movie filtering interfaces.
    

# Note

- Does not require a search query (`query`).
    
- Supports over **30 filtering and sorting parameters**.
    
- Returns results in a paginated format.
    
- Multiple filters can be combined to create highly specific searches.
    
- Each movie includes a TMDB movie ID you can use with the Movie collection to retrieve detailed information.
    

**Note:** This endpoint supports more than 30 query parameters. The parameters listed above are the most commonly used. Refer to the TMDB API reference for the complete list of supported filters and sorting options.

request.description:
Discovers TV shows by applying one or more filtering and sorting criteria instead of a search query.

> **Note**: This endpoint retrieves public TMDB data and does not require a `session_id` or `account_id`. 
  

# Query parameters

| Parameter | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | Specifies the language of the returned results. | `en-US` |
| `sort_by` | Sorts the results using a supported sort option. | `popularity.desc` |
| `page` | Returns a specific page of results. | `1` |
| `with_genres` | Filters TV shows by one or more genre IDs. | `18,10765` |
| `first_air_date_year` | Filters TV shows by the year they first aired. | `2024` |
| `vote_average.gte` | Returns TV shows with at least the specified average rating. | `8` |
| `vote_count.gte` | Returns TV shows with at least the specified number of votes. | `100` |
| `with_original_language` | Filters TV shows by their original language. | `en` |
| `with_watch_providers` | Filters TV shows available on specific streaming providers. | `8` |
| `watch_region` | Specifies the country used for watch provider filtering. | `US` |

## Request example

```
GET {{base_url}}/discover/tv?with_genres=18&first_air_date_year=2024&sort_by=popularity.desc

 ```

# Example response

``` json
{
  "page": 1,
  "results": [
    {
      "adult": false,
      "backdrop_path": "/xUB3xFMgsHgPmdWnUWkHTJ03vHa.jpg",
      "genre_ids": [10759, 10765, 18, 10751],
      "id": 82452,
      "origin_country": ["US"],
      "original_language": "en",
      "original_name": "Avatar: The Last Airbender",
      "overview": "A young boy known as the Avatar must master the four elemental powers to save a world at war...",
      "popularity": 169.5136,
      "poster_path": "/lzZpWEaqzP0qVA5nkCc5ASbNcSy.jpg",
      "first_air_date": "2024-02-22",
      "softcore": false,
      "name": "Avatar: The Last Airbender",
      "vote_average": 7.789,
      "vote_count": 1255
    }
  ],
  "total_pages": 148,
  "total_results": 2951
}

 ```

# Response field

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | Integer | The current page number. |
| `results` | Array | Contains TV shows that match the specified filters. |
| `results[].adult` | Boolean | Indicates whether the TV show is classified as adult content. |
| `results[].backdrop_path` | String / null | The relative path to the TV show's backdrop image. |
| `results[].genre_ids` | Array | Contains the TMDB genre IDs associated with the TV show. |
| `results[].id` | Integer | The unique TMDB ID of the TV show. |
| `results[].origin_country` | Array | Contains the country codes associated with the TV show's origin. |
| `results[].original_language` | String | The original language of the TV show. |
| `results[].original_name` | String | The original name of the TV show. |
| `results[].overview` | String | A brief description of the TV show. |
| `results[].popularity` | Number | The TV show's popularity score on TMDB. |
| `results[].poster_path` | String / null | The relative path to the TV show's poster image. |
| `results[].first_air_date` | String | The date the TV show first aired, in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. |
| `results[].softcore` | Boolean | Indicates whether the TV show is classified as softcore content. |
| `results[].name` | String | The name of the TV show. |
| `results[].vote_average` | Number | The average user rating for the TV show. |
| `results[].vote_count` | Integer | The number of votes received by the TV show. |
| `total_pages` | Integer | The total number of pages available. |
| `total_results` | Integer | The total number of TV shows matching the specified filters. |

# TV-specific filtering

The Discover TV endpoint shares many filtering options with **Discover Movies**, but it also includes parameters specific to television content.

| Discover Movies | Discover TV |
| --- | --- |
| `primary_release_year` | `first_air_date_year` |
| `primary_release_date.gte` | `first_air_date.gte` |
| `primary_release_date.lte` | `first_air_date.lte` |

Use `first_air_date_year` when you want to retrieve TV shows that premiered during a specific year.

For example:

```
GET {{base_url}}/discover/tv?first_air_date_year=2024

 ```

This request returns TV shows whose first episode aired in **2024**.

# AND / OR Filter Logic

Several filtering parameters support combining multiple values using commas (`,`) or pipes (`|`).

| Separator | Behavior | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `,` | **AND** — results must satisfy all specified values. | `with_genres=18,10765` |
| \` | \` | **OR** — results may satisfy any specified value. |

For example:

- `with_genres=18,10765` returns TV shows that are both **Drama** and **Sci-Fi & Fantasy**.
    
- `with_genres=18|10765` returns TV shows that are **Drama** or **Sci-Fi & Fantasy**.
    

# Common use cases

- Build **Browse TV Shows** pages.
    
- Recommend TV series based on genres or ratings.
    
- Filter TV shows by language, streaming provider, or first air date.
    
- Display popular, top-rated, or recently premiered TV series.
    
- Create advanced filtering experiences for television content.
    

# Note

- Does not require a search query (`query`).
    
- Supports advanced filtering and sorting through multiple query parameters.
    
- Returns results in a paginated format.
    
- Multiple filters can be combined to create highly specific discovery queries.
    
- Each TV show includes a unique TMDB TV series ID that can be used with the TV collection to retrieve additional information.
    

**Note:** The Discover TV endpoint supports many of the same filtering and sorting options as **Discover Movies**. However, TV-specific parameters such as `first_air_date_year`, `first_air_date.gte`, and `first_air_date.lte` replace the movie-specific release date parameters. Use the endpoint that corresponds to the type of media you want to discover.

item.description:
The **Discover** collection contains endpoints for retrieving movies and TV shows using advanced filtering, sorting, and discovery criteria. Unlike the **Search** collection, which requires a user-provided search term, the Discover endpoints allow applications to browse TMDB's catalog by applying filters such as genres, release dates, ratings, popularity, certifications, watch providers, original language, and many other attributes.

Since the Discover collection retrieves publicly available TMDB data, these endpoints do not require user-specific authentication, such as a `session_id` or `account_id`.

# Purpose

The Discover collection supports the following operations:

- Discover movies using multiple filtering criteria.
    
- Discover TV shows using advanced search filters.
    
- Filter content by genre, language, release date, certification, runtime, popularity, vote average, and vote count.
    
- Sort results by popularity, release date, rating, revenue, and other supported fields.
    
- Browse results using pagination.
    
- Build personalized recommendation and content browsing experiences.
    

# Common query parameters

Although supported parameters vary between endpoints, the following are commonly used throughout the Discover collection.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `language` | Specifies the language of the returned results. |
| `page` | Returns a specific page of results. |
| `sort_by` | Sorts results using supported sorting options. |
| `with_genres` | Filters content by one or more genres. |
| `with_watch_providers` | Filters content available from specific streaming providers. |
| `watch_region` | Specifies the country used for watch provider filtering. |
| `vote_average.gte` | Returns content with a minimum average rating. |
| `vote_count.gte` | Returns content with a minimum number of votes. |
| `primary_release_year` | Filters movies by release year. |
| `first_air_date_year` | Filters TV shows by first air date year. |
| `with_original_language` | Filters content by its original language. |

# Common use cases

The endpoints in this collection can be used for the following functionalities:

- Build Browse Movies and Browse TV Shows pages.
    
- Recommend content based on genres and ratings.
    
- Create "Top Rated," "Popular," or "Recently Released" sections.
    
- Filter content available from specific streaming providers.
    
- Generate personalized content recommendations.
    
- Build advanced filtering interfaces.
    

## Search vs. Discover

| Search | Discover |
| --- | --- |
| Requires a search term (`query`). | Does not require a search term. |
| Finds content by title or name. | Finds content using filters and sorting criteria. |
| Best for users who know what they are looking for. | Best for browsing and exploring content. |
| Returns keyword-based matches. | Returns content matching specified filters. |

**Tip:** Use the **Search** endpoints when users know the title or name of the content they want to find. Use the **Discover** endpoints when users want to browse or filter content based on attributes such as genre, release date, popularity, ratings, streaming providers, or language.
